business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration through in-house design & development (complete design lifecycle - mechanical/electrical system design, control architecture and simulation) using tools such as E-PLAN, SolidWorks, AutoCAD and ZW Cad, and in-house assembly, testing and quality assurance at the MIDC Bhosari, Pune assembly unit (co-located inventory to minimize material movement). Automation-solutions revenue is project-based and integrated end-to-end, while a trading stream procures automation products (PLC, HMI, Servo, AC Drive, digital picking system components) from various suppliers and delivers them in original form. Major raw materials are sourced indigenously, predominantly from Maharashtra (79.45%, 70.98%, 78.82% and 83.83% of total raw material purchases for period ended Oct 31, 2025 and FY2025, FY2024, FY2023). No long-term supply contracts with suppliers. Forward-side lifecycle support includes 12-month warranty, repair/replacement, system upgrades, retrofitting, AMC and on-site installation, commissioning and troubleshooting.

concerns_observed: Weak earnings-to-cash conversion: operating cash flow was negative in two of three fiscals - Rs (641.32) lakh (FY24) and Rs (72.47) lakh (FY25) - despite rising PAT; FY25 trade receivables of Rs 5,613.24 lakh equalled 42.62% of revenue.
Heavy automotive-sector dependence: the automotive segment was 59.95% / 78.61% / 72.48% / 64.32% of revenue (Oct'25 stub / FY25 / FY24 / FY23), tying demand to auto-industry capex cycles.
Customer concentration with no long-term contracts: top customer 43.39-50.86%, top 5 customers 62.21-67.40% and top 10 customers 70.18-77.19% of revenue across the reported periods.
Supplier concentration: top 10 suppliers were 76.57-85.54% of raw-material purchases and Maharashtra sourcing 70.98-83.83%, with no long-term supply contracts.
Geographic concentration - Haryana 51.05-64.20% and Maharashtra ~30% of revenue - and a single Pune assembly unit; the registered office, assembly unit and two sales/service offices are all rented.
Rising share of lower-margin trading of automation products (23.68% of revenue in FY23 to 38.69% in the Oct'25 stub) may dilute blended margins versus the customised-solutions business.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration through in-house design & development (complete design lifecycle - mechanical/electrical system design, control architecture and simulation) using tools such as E-PLAN, SolidWorks, AutoCAD and ZW Cad, and in-house assembly, testing and quality assurance at the MIDC Bhosari, Pune assembly unit (co-located inventory to minimize material movement). Automation-solutions revenue is project-based and integrated end-to-end, while a trading stream procures automation products (PLC, HMI, Servo, AC Drive, digital picking system components) from various suppliers and delivers them in original form. Major raw materials are sourced indigenously, predominantly from Maharashtra (79.45%, 70.98%, 78.82% and 83.83% of total raw material purchases for period ended Oct 31, 2025 and FY2025, FY2024, FY2023). No long-term supply contracts with suppliers. Forward-side lifecycle support includes 12-month warranty, repair/replacement, system upgrades, retrofitting, AMC and on-site installation, commissioning and troubleshooting.

moat.body:

- Integrated in-house assembling and testing infrastructure under one roof at MIDC Bhosari, Pune
- Enduring relationships with a diversified customer base across more than 10 states in India; ~279 customers served in FY25
- Experienced promoters (28 and 12 years) and skilled employees

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration — Top 10 customers contributed ~74.09% and top 5 ~63.85% of revenue in FY25; loss of a key customer could materially impact revenue
- End-market concentration in automotive — Automotive vertical accounted for ~78.61% of FY25 sales, exposing the company to automotive-sector cyclicality
- Geographic concentration — Haryana (56.10%) and Maharashtra (29.57%) together made up the bulk of FY25 sales
- Execution/expansion risk on new factory — Growth depends on timely establishment and shifting of operations to the new IPO-funded Pimpri factory unit
- Promoter and key-personnel dependence — Business relies heavily on promoters Ajay and Preeti Prabhu and a small design/engineering team
- Working-capital intensity and borrowings — Total borrowings of Rs 1,968.21 lakhs as at Oct 31, 2025; a portion of IPO proceeds and working capital funding is required to support the project-based order book
- Certification not yet obtained — ISO 9001:2015 certification only applied for (Stage 2 audit scheduled May 2026), not yet received
